messages:
Anika: Quick heads-up — noticed a weird split after the quota routing change. /v1/generate p95 down ~40ms but p99 up ~220ms for the same endpoint :eyes:
Sanjay: Are those from the same client cohort? Could be fallback routing mixing faster small payloads with some slow long-tail requests
Anika: Good q — I sliced by caller tag and it looks mixed. Most traffic from 'mobile-prod' moved to the quota path, but p99 jump seems to come from requests that hit a different pool (maybe non-quantized nodes)
Wei: Did the routing policy change also change route weights or the pool selection predicate? ops-bot shows a config apply at 6120001200
ops-bot: Routing policy apply: policy=quota_fallback_v2 by devops@infra — changed weight for pool=reserved->shared (6120001200)
Jules: Can we validate by breaking percentiles per sample_origin (client vs router vs pool) + kv_cache_hit? Quick query: ```SELECT sample_origin, pool, quant_mode, p50(lat_ms), p95(lat_ms), p99(lat_ms) FROM requests WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate' AND ts>now()-2h GROUP BY sample_origin, pool, quant_mode```
Anika: I ran something similar — sample_origin shows both "direct" and "fallback_quota". Most fallback_quota p95 is better but p99 is dominated by pool=shared-nodegroup-7
Sanjay: That suggests a capacity or perf heterogeneity in the shared pool. Two asks: 1) annotate dashboard with sample_origin breakdown (small toggle), 2) make routing telemetry include pool_id + quant_mode in the rollup metrics
console-ui: We can add a temporary toggle in the dashboard to split by sample_origin, but backend needs to surface sample_origin tag at aggregation time. Adding toggle will require a new query param to the backend: `split_by=sample_origin`
Wei: Also watch cardinality — do not let pool_id explode the legend. Maybe expose pool_id only as a top-5 breakdown and 'other' bucket
Jules: Agreed. For now the dashboard toggle should default to 3 buckets: direct, fallback_quota, other. If backend supports pool_id we can surface heatmap drilldown next
Anika: Short-term mitigation: can we bias routing back to reserved for mobile-prod while we investigate? That should lower p99 immediately for that client cohort
Sanjay: We can push a quick canary revert for mobile-prod routing weight. Will coordinate with infra to avoid thrash :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Canary rollout: routing_weight_override for client=mobile-prod -> reserved +20% (started 6120001255)
console-ui: Filing follow-up: UI ticket to add `split_by` toggle + backend contract to return `sample_origin` and `pool_summary` fields. I'll link the ticket here once created
Anika: Thanks all. Action items: Sanjay to run canary revert, Jules/Wei to run percentile-by-pool query and share top N offenders, console-ui to create UI + backend ticket. Ping me when queries land. :shipit:
